title: Probe prioritization affinity and retirement notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes to standardize how we prioritize probes (synthetic checks, metrics, spans) for multi-tenant inference and when/ how we retire legacy metrics. This is meant to be pragmatic: reduce operator noise, bound query cost, and preserve investigation fidelity for P1 customer incidents.

Background/context:
- Over the last 6 months we've accumulated ~140 small probes across dashboards and alerting. Many overlap or are low-signal for actual customer impact.
- Common pain: dashboards with slow queries, flaky alerts, and trace sampling that doesn’t attach to the right token/session context.
- This doc sketches an affinity-based prioritization approach, retirement criteria, and a small migration plan for the Q4 telemetry cleanup.

Affinity Matrix (how to prioritize):
Axis definitions:
- User Impact (High/Med/Low): Does this probe/metric directly map to customer-visible failure modes (e.g., TTF token spikes, 5xxs, KV cache miss storms)?
- Signal Cost (High/Med/Low): Cost to run and to retain (query cost, cardinality, trace volume).
- Investigability Multiplier (+/-): Does this probe materially speed up RCA (session stitching, trace anchors, prompt replay)?

Priority buckets (rule-of-thumb):
- P0 (keep, refine): High User Impact + Low/Med Signal Cost + Positive Investigability
- P1 (keep, but optimize): High User Impact + High Signal Cost OR Med Impact + Low Cost + High Investigability
- P2 (de-duplicate/merge): Med/Low Impact + Med/High Cost but overlaps with P0/P1 signals
- P3 (retire or sandbox): Low Impact + High Cost + Low Investigability

Metric retirement criteria (must meet all to retire):
1) No linked incidents in last 180 days OR only noise-only incidents (operator false positives)
2) Metric has < 5 queries/month from dashboards/alerts (after a 30d sampling)
3) There exists an alternative signal that covers the same hypothesis with better cost profile (e.g., bucketed quantile panel or synthetic probe)
4) Product/CS stake holders sign-off if metric was customer-facing (email thread or Jira ticket)

Tracing anchors and span design notes:
- Always attach a top-level cross-tenant session id: session_id or request_session. This is required for multi-hop inference traces to be reconstructed.
- For model fanout (multi-model routing), include fields: route_variant, model_id, batch_size, kv_warmth_flag. Keep them low-cardinality (map large strings to short codes).
- Event anchors: producer.start, model.fetch, kv.read, kv.evict, runtime.forward, runtime.token_emit. These named anchors simplify timeline slicing.
- Sampling guidance: keep 100% sampling for P0 incidents for 24h post-incident; otherwise adaptive 1% baseline but proportional to tenant weight.
- Span size control: for long-lived sessions ( > 5s ) prefer chunked spans per 1s slice to avoid large trace payloads.

Dashboard widget split & query-throttle rules:
- Rule: Never put a high-cardinality list (tenant_id, full-prompt-text) directly in an expensive panel. Use derived low-cardinality tags (tenant_tier, prompt_type).
- Split slow panels: heavy histograms or quantile scans should be moved to an async microdash that runs hourly, with a lightweight overview panel in the main dashboard.
- Query throttle pattern: autoscale query frequency by dashboard viewers: default 5m, power-users can opt-in to 1m. Add a note in the dashboard description explaining costs.
- Widget TTL: mark panels with a documented TTL (live, hourly, daily). Panels set to 'hourly' can safely use larger lookbacks.

Migration plan (phases):
Phase 0 - audit (2 weeks): inventory all probes and owners, annotate each with UserImpact/SignalCost/Investigability. Use a simple sheet for scoring.
Phase 1 - quick wins (2 weeks): remove duplicate low-cost panels, set sampling on noisy spans, add session_id where missing.
Phase 2 - retire P3s (3 weeks): communicate retire schedule, add redirects in dashboards to replacement signals, archive queries for 90 days.
Phase 3 - optimize P1 (ongoing): replace heavy metrics with compact quantile panels or synthetic probes, and instrument trace anchors for RCA.

Operational runbook snippets:
- If a new noisy alert appears: triage owner adds it to "alerts-noise" board, flip sampling to 0.1% for 24h and annotate. If no meaningful alerts in 7d -> retire.
- On incident opener: enable 100% trace sampling for tenants impacted for 48h; spin up temporary microdash with heavy analysis panels.

Quick todo (who/when):
- Marcus: run inventory export of dashboards and alerts (due 2025-11-10)
- Aisha: draft retire announcement + Slack template for affected teams (due 2025-11-14)
- Dmitri: add session_id enrichment shim into the agent SDK (PR target 2025-11-21)
- Leah: coordinate sign-offs and update the metric catalog after Phase 0 (due 2025-12-01)

Decision log & open questions:
- Decision: default adaptive trace sampling baseline 1% (approved by eng-observability 2025-10-28).
- Open: Should we use token-level anonymized hashes in traces for prompt attribution? (privacy/legal check needed)
- Open: exact SLA for archiving retired query results (30d vs 90d) - propose 90d for 2026 trial.

Notes & references:
- See linked artifacts for the inventory sheet and the E2E session stitching RFC.
- Example Slack thread: #obs-telemetry-cleanup-2025 (searchable)

Appendix: scoring rubric (short)
- UserImpact: 3=customer-visible, 2=team-visible, 1=informational
- SignalCost: 3=high (heavy queries / wide cardinality), 2=medium, 1=low
- Investigability: 1=adds <1min to RCA, 2=adds 1-5min, 3=adds >5min (higher is better)

End of notes. Please add items inline; the plan assumes collaboration and a week-by-week check-in during the cleanup sprint.
